items.label: Plan how you will disclose AI use
items.what: Plan how you will disclose AI use in publications, presentations, and to participants.
items.why: Most journals and conferences now require AI disclosure. Transparency builds trust and is increasingly required by publishers.
items.how: Draft a disclosure statement describing which AI tools were used and for what purpose. Include in your methods section.

items.label: Check AI grades for fairness
items.what: Verify AI grading produces equitable outcomes across student demographics.
items.why: AI grading tools can carry biases from training data, leading to unfair outcomes for certain student groups.
items.how: Compare AI-generated grades across demographic subgroups. Check for statistically significant disparities. Document findings and any corrections made.

items.label: Check whether FERPA applies to this data
items.what: Confirm student records processed by AI are handled per FERPA requirements.
items.why: Student education records are protected under FERPA. Sending them to external AI services may violate federal law.
items.how: Check that AI processing happens on institution-approved systems. Check vendor data processing agreements. Confirm no student data is retained by third-party AI services.

items.label: Share grading criteria with students
items.what: Ensure students are informed that AI is used in the grading process.
items.why: Students have a right to know how their work is evaluated. Transparency builds trust and meets institutional policy requirements.
items.how: Update your syllabus to include AI grading disclosure. Communicate in class and provide an opt-out or appeal mechanism if required by policy.

items.label: Decide how you will override AI grades
items.what: Define a process for students to appeal or request human review of AI-assisted grades.
items.why: Students must have recourse when they believe an AI grade is incorrect. This is both an ethical and often institutional requirement.
items.how: Establish a clear appeal window (e.g., 7 days). Document the process in the syllabus. Ensure a human instructor reviews all appeals.

items.label: Spot-check AI grades against your own
items.what: Sample and validate AI-generated grades against instructor judgment.
items.why: AI grading must be verified for accuracy before being applied at scale. Unvalidated AI grades risk harming student outcomes.
items.how: Review a random 20-25% sample of AI grades. Compare with your own assessment. Document agreement rate and any adjustments made.

items.label: Check that the data is de-identified
items.what: Ensure personal identifiers are removed before AI processing.
items.why: Sending identifiable data to AI systems (especially cloud-based) may violate privacy regulations and IRB requirements.
items.how: Remove or mask: names, dates, locations, ID numbers, photos, and any combination that could identify someone. Use established de-identification standards (HIPAA Safe Harbor or Expert Determination).
